God would not destroy towns unjustly while inhabitants reform; no specific earlier source authenticated.
Counterfactual unity of humankind and continuing disagreement; compare only as a broad theological motif.

dossier.title: Reformers, disagreement, mercy and the purpose of prophetic narratives
dossier.chronological_background: These verses conclude the extended historical warnings in Hūd and explain how accounts of previous messengers serve admonition and reassurance.
dossier.similarities: General themes of communal reform, disagreement, judgment and exemplary recollection occur in several late antique religious traditions, but none is authenticated here as a verse-specific textual parallel.
dossier.differences: Q11:119 explicitly joins jinn and humans in an eschatological statement; Q11:120 describes the narratives' consolatory function for Muhammad. Do not project these formulations onto earlier texts.
dossier.variant_witnesses: No Hebrew, Greek, Syriac, or Arabic manuscript witnesses collated in this preliminary batch.
dossier.dating: No external composition or manuscript dates assigned without passage-level identification.
dossier.interpretations: Independent ethical exhortation, shared regional discourse, and scriptural intertextuality remain distinct hypotheses; none has been established for these verses.
